title: PeerReview
description: Output of Phase 4. The dispatched panel roles review the diff (all six at architectural/trivial tier; ba+dev+qa+secops plus surface-conditional dba/devops at standard tier, per status.json panel_roles). Orchestrator merges the per-role shards and computes final_verdict. Only dispatched roles appear as keys; an absent role key means trimmed-by-tier, never a missing review. APPROVE_WITH_NOTES is canonical; APPROVE_WITH_NITS is a legacy alias kept valid for archived runs. THIS WHOLE FILE IS ARCHIVED INTO A COMMITTED TREE. peer-review is in knowledge-store.mjs's ARCHIVE_ARTIFACTS, so Phase 5 folds it into knowledge/issue-archive/<n>.json, which is tracked and public; only a LEADING absolute-path span is rewritten on the way. Every free-text field below therefore carries the same no-credential rule, and the per-field notes are the STATEMENT of it, not the control: #71 sites the control at the archive write, where the walk is over the whole assembled document and so covers fields no schema declares (advisory_notes on the design and art-director blocks, the string leaves of knowledge_drift_claims) and fields nobody has written yet. THE HALF THAT IS STILL A NORM: the control matches enumerated credential SHAPES, so a secret spelled as prose reaches the tree, and a fix-forward commit does not remove it from history - the remedy is to AMEND.

verdict.description: REQUEST_REFACTOR is QA-only (testability). VETO is SecOps-only.

severity.description: This schema is the single source of truth for concern severity. The canonical panel vocabulary is blocker|major|nit (DBA/DevOps/Design emit these); SecOps's CVE-style critical|high|medium|low|info is accepted alongside it so a SecOps concern (e.g. severity 'low') validates cleanly. Distinct from the knowledge_drift_claims severity field.

description.description: THE SHARP CASE for the archive rule that follows, and the same shape #52 named on status.json's `error`: the natural content of a concern description is COPIED MACHINE OUTPUT - a failed command echoing a token-bearing URL, a DSN out of a connection error, an .env line inside a stack trace. That is how credential material gets into a review artifact at all, and a Phase 4 panel reviewing an actual diff is quoting tool output constantly. ARCHIVED VERBATIM into the committed knowledge/issue-archive/<n>.json; only a LEADING absolute-path span is rewritten on the way (redactAbsolutePaths in knowledge-store.mjs). NEVER PASTE CREDENTIAL MATERIAL HERE - a fix-forward commit does not remove a secret from a public history, so the remedy is to AMEND. Since #71 a CONTROL backs that rule and not only a norm: archiveIssue walks the whole assembled archive and REFUSES the write on a credential-shaped string, naming the json path and the class (override PIPELINE_ARCHIVE_ALLOW_CREDENTIAL_SHAPES, never silent). It matches enumerated SHAPES, so a secret spelled as prose passes it and you are still the control that matters. And the instrument is CONTENT, not length: do not cap this field, a long description recording a live reproduction is correct work.

must_satisfy.description: What a correct fix must BE TRUE OF, carrying in itself the observation whose outcome decides whether it is met - never HOW to make it true. A mechanism you weighed goes in rationale_not_checked. TWO ROLES ARE EXEMPT, recorded here because the rule is unreadable without it: QA and Dev own solution design through the TDD contract, so a QA or Dev concern that specifies a test, a matrix or a mechanism is IN BOUNDS, and this field is where it goes. TYPED HERE AND UNENFORCED HERE, deliberately: this subschema has NO required list, and must_satisfy is not being added to one, because adding one turns the shipped self-test in scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs from 68 passed / 0 failed to 65 passed / 3 failed. The three cases that would redden are 'panel major severity accepted', 'panel concern severity low accepted (CVE-style)' and 'panel concern severity critical accepted (CVE-style)'; they live in validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs, which this change may not edit. Tracked in #38. So a Phase 4 reviewer who writes a mechanism here gets no pushback from any machine today. (a) WHERE A MISSING PROPERTY IS REFUSED, none of it in this file, and stated over the PAIR that decides it - the STOPPING AGENT'S TYPE and the artifact - because a location alone decides nothing: three agent types are refused, dba, devops and secops, on concerns[] in review.schema.json and on remediation in SecOps vulnerabilities[]. THE ARTIFACT SET IS TWO FILES PER TYPE, NOT ONE: reviewerRules gives each of those three both its own review.<role>.json shard AND the MERGED review.json at /<role> (validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:86-89 lists the four rules; :88 is the merged one), so the refusal is keyed to the STOP and not to the moment of writing. A merged Phase 2 record is re-read at every later stop of the same type while its mtime is inside the 30-minute window, which is how a Phase 4 reviewer gets blocked on a Phase 2 block it did not write. MEASURED ON THIS CHANGE'S OWN RUN, roots = repo root, active issue 40: checkArtifacts returns 4 failures for dba, 2 for devops and 5 for secops, every one of them 'review.json/<role> /concerns[N]: missing required field "must_satisfy"' on rows written in Phase 2 before this contract existed; ba, dev, librarian, design and art-director return none at all in the same run, and qa returns none on review.json - its 4 are on peer-review.json, for a severity value outside that enum, which is a different defect in a different file. That partition is the non-zero control: the fixture is not simply blocking everything. WHAT TO DO WHEN IT HAPPENS: let the file age past the 30-minute window, or re-run the Phase 2 reviewer that owns the block. Do NOT backfill a property into another role's finished record, and least of all '', which writes a property nobody stated into a record that is about to be archived. README 'Upgrading' item 14 says the same thing to an operator deciding whether to upgrade mid-run. NO OTHER AGENT TYPE IS REFUSED ON ANY PHASE 2 ARTIFACT: design and art-director have no AGENT_RULES entry at all, and ba, dev, qa and librarian have entries that reach no review shard, so Design - a real Phase 2 reviewer - writes an unvalidated one. NOT on SecOps compliance_flags[], whose items subschema has no required list at all - a VETO with no statute, no concern and no action validates SILENT. NOT on any Phase 4 peer-review artifact, which is this one (#38). (b) THE ENFORCEMENT RECORD IS DATED AND SCOPED BY DEPLOYMENT MODE, never by repository identity. WINDOW: measured 2026-08-21. POPULATION, with its inclusion rule stated because the corpus is larger than the count: one machine's ~/.claude/projects, walked RECURSIVELY - subagent transcripts live in per-session SUBDIRECTORIES, and a top-level-only walk sees 82 of 1680 files and finds ZERO blocks, which is output-identical to the finding it is supposed to test. 13 repositories in that corpus hold any transcript; the 8 counted here are those carrying pipeline activity of either kind, at least one block or at least one namespaced dispatch, and they held 1638 files / 353,907 lines when this was written. THE CORPUS IS LIVE AND ONLY GROWS: re-run hours later it reads 1680 files / 366,314 lines over all 13, and 1662 / 362,734 over the 8. What must reproduce is the partition, not the absolute. FINDING: 56 genuine blocks, every one of them in a project that dispatches BARE agent names from local .claude/agents/*.md files; ZERO across 670 plugin-namespaced dispatches in SEVEN repositories - 645 of them excluding the 25 this change's own session had recorded when the figure was taken - one of which is an adopting project directory with 362. ONE COUNTING RULE FOR BOTH FIGURES, pipeline agents only, and MIND THE GRAIN: at the recipe's project-directory grain that adopting directory shows 362 and its other-plugin set is EMPTY. The 365 belongs to the REPOSITORY grain, which sums that directory with a second project directory for the same repository where 3 dispatches of another plugin's agent live; that plugin's agent is one this hook could not have refused under any repair. Two grains, two numbers, and the recipe below states only the first. RE-DERIVATION, and run it rather than reading it: walk every *.jsonl under ~/.claude/projects RECURSIVELY (the subagent transcripts are in subdirectories), count messages whose message.content is a plain string beginning 'Stop hook feedback:\nPipeline artifact failed schema validation', group by project directory; then cross-tabulate against the subagent_type field of the recorded subagent-dispatch tool_use entries, selecting those entries by tool name IN ('Task','Agent'). BOTH NAMES, and this is the step that decides whether the paragraph re-derives at all: on the corpus above the host recorded 'Agent' 1623 times, rising with every session run since, and 'Task' ZERO times, so a cross-tabulation keyed on 'Task' alone comes back EMPTY in every repository - output-identical to the zero-blocks finding it is supposed to test. ITS NON-ZERO CONTROL: the dispatch count must come back non-zero before any zero-block figure means anything; if it does not, your selector missed the tool rather than the corpus missing the dispatches. Then run the four-cell agent_type fixture ('secops', 'SecOps', 'pipeline:secops', 'agent-pipeline:secops') against the shipped hook. The installed plugin with namespaced names is the shipping default, so read this as a dated record and not as a warranty for your deployment. AND EVERY ENFORCEMENT CLAIM HERE DESCRIBES THE SOURCE TREE at that date: an installed plugin runs its own cached copy of these schemas and of the agent contracts until that installation is refreshed, so a claim true on the integration branch is not yet true in a session running the cache. Filed as #66; the correct outcome for #66 is that somebody fixes it, on which day this paragraph becomes false and a silence has no event that notices. (c) THE FAIL-OPEN DEGRADATIONS, five of them: the enforced half degrades to nothing when node is absent, when the plugin root is unset, when the active issue is unresolvable, when the artifact's mtime exceeds 30 minutes, and - dominantly, and this is the one that screens off the other four - when the stopping agent's type does not match an AGENT_RULES key (validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:93 for the keys, :654-656 for the lookup and its early return). (d) THE EMPTY STRING SATISFIES, wherever the field IS required: the walker implements no minLength and the requirement cannot be conditioned on severity. Measured 2026-08-21 over the bare-name deployments where the gate fires, and that population is stated as a RULE YOU CAN RUN rather than as a list of checkouts, because 'the deployments where it fires' is not walkable while a list of names would scope this record by IDENTITY, which (b) forbids for exactly the reason it would be wrong here too - identity is an accident of one machine, the deployment mode is the property. THE RULE: enumerate every checkout under the projects root and keep the ones whose .claude/agents/ directory holds THIS pipeline's own agent files by name (ba, dba, devops, secops, dev, qa, librarian, design, art-director). On the machine this was measured on, exactly TWO checkouts qualify; three further checkouts carry local agents that are NOT this pipeline's and dispatch namespaced, and the same rule excludes them without a judgement call. That is a DIFFERENT and much larger population than the knowledge/issue-archive/ folder beside this schema: 17 of 229 already-written vulnerability rows there carry no remediation - info 9, low 4, medium 4, and ZERO of the 3 critical and ZERO of the 26 high. Counting the local archive will not reproduce that denominator and is not meant to. HOW THE 229 WAS REACHED, because a reader who gets a different number will blame the record rather than the glob, and each near miss below is one a reader actually hit: EVERY .pipeline directory in those two checkouts was walked, including the ones under .claude/worktrees, and vulnerabilities[] was counted in BOTH artifact families. The top-level .pipeline directories alone give 101 rows and 16 without remediation; the review family alone gives 210 and 16, because 19 of the 229 rows sit in peer-review files and 1 of the 17 with them. Concerns rows count only entries that are OBJECTS - 9 non-object entries, all in the peer family, are excluded, and one file in the corpus does not parse at all. AND UNLIKE THE CORPUS IN (b), THIS ONE CAN SHRINK: it is counted over working checkouts whose .claude/worktrees get PRUNED, so growth is not the only direction and a later walk can land BELOW every denominator here. Read a smaller number as the population moving; read a changed PARTITION as the record drifting. THAT 17-OF-229 IS ONE HALF OF THIS MIGRATION; THE OTHER HALF IS 100%, and a reader who takes 7% away as the retroactive scale has the wrong number. Same population, same walk, same day: 996 already-written concerns rows, not one of them carrying must_satisfy. Against the merge-base required list [severity, description], 185 of 996 fail; against the shipped list [severity, description, must_satisfy], 996 of 996 fail. MIND THE GRAIN ON BOTH, because those 996 span two artifact families with different contracts. 488 sit in review.json and review.<role>.json, which agentBlock's required list governs: 0 of those 488 failed the merge-base list and 488 of 488 fail the shipped one, so on the population this change actually governs the already-written failing fraction moves from 0% to 100%. The other 508 sit in peer-review.json and peer-review.<role>.json, whose items subschema has no required list at all (#38) - every one of the 185 merge-base failures is in that half, and none of them is refused by anything. None of those rows is revalidated once its file passes the 30-minute window; what IS revalidated is a merged review.json in a run still in flight, which clause (a) measures and states. The empty-string residual itself moved to #122 when #71 closed: #71 carried BOTH halves and shipped only the credential one, so the wider class of free-text reviewer fields crossing the archived-and-committed boundary is now covered (every free-text field on both review schemas carries the rule, and archiveIssue refuses a credential-shaped write) while the empty-string half is not. #122 states why: the only write-time seat for a non-blank check is validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs, which #66 records as inert under namespaced dispatch - the shipping default - so a control placed there would be green about the deployment mode rather than about the record. (e) THE ARCHIVE RESIDUAL. What you write here is copied verbatim into knowledge/issue-archive/<n>.json, which IS committed, and that copy runs through the absolute-path redactor in knowledge-store.mjs. A property that OPENS with a route is rewritten: origin/main today carries LEADING_SPAN (knowledge-store.mjs:147), which replaces the leading path span only and leaves the prose after it standing; the earlier ABSOLUTE_VALUE form replaced the WHOLE value, prose and all. The invariant true under BOTH forms, and the only one to rely on, is that a LEADING path span does not survive into the durable record - so put the route mid-sentence or the archived property loses its subject. Check which form is live rather than trusting this sentence: grep -n 'ABSOLUTE_VALUE\|LEADING_SPAN' plugins/pipeline/scripts/knowledge-store.mjs. Because that copy is verbatim and public, never paste credential material into this field - and read that as a rule you honor, not a control that protects you -- AND #71 CHANGED HALF OF THAT, so read the rest of this sentence as its correction. There is still no length check and deliberately none, because the instrument is CONTENT and not length. There IS now a pattern check: archiveIssue walks the whole assembled archive and REFUSES the write on a credential-shaped string, naming the json path and the class, overridable only through PIPELINE_ARCHIVE_ALLOW_CREDENTIAL_SHAPES and never silently. It matches enumerated SHAPES, so a secret spelled as prose still validates clean and is archived as written, and you are still the control that matters. (f) THE NEIGHBOUR LIMIT. This annotation warrants nothing beyond its own field. It warrants NOTHING about the concern severity enum beside it: 10 already-archived panel rows carry values outside that enum, and nothing here changes whether they validate. It warrants NOTHING about this file's root required list, which is [final_verdict, reviewed_at] - verified at the merge base - because no AGENT_RULES entry targets the document root, so that list has no validation path at all. (g) THIS SUBSCHEMA IS DELIBERATELY OPEN, and no check in this repository enforces that. Neither it nor the other two subschemas this change edited (SecOps vulnerabilities[].items in review.schema.json, panelVerdict concerns[].items in peer-review.schema.json) declares additionalProperties, and that openness is what makes the added required field REVERSIBLE: an instance written under the new contract, carrying keys the old one never declared, still validates against the pre-change schemas. Closing any of the three turns a reversible addition into a one-way migration on the day these artifacts meet a conformant validator. DO NOT READ THAT AS A GUARDED INVARIANT: the shipped walker implements no additionalProperties keyword at all - it handles type, enum, required, properties, minItems, items and allOf - so planting additionalProperties:false on any of the three reddens nothing: not the self-test, not the hook, not the suite. It is a written invariant with no enforcement, recorded here because here is where the next editor of this subschema is looking.

knowledge_drift_claims.description: Optional staleness claims for the Librarian, recorded INSIDE the block (never as a sibling key beside it). ITS STRING LEAVES ARE UNDECLARED (store_says, live_reality, evidence) and they are free text quoting live state, so they are exactly the fields a per-field credential note can never reach - and they are ARCHIVED VERBATIM like everything else here. That is the reason the #71 control is sited at the archive write over the whole assembled document rather than on the fields: `evidence` here and `advisory_notes` on the design/art-director blocks are both archived, and neither is declared in any schema, so neither could ever have carried a note. NEVER PASTE CREDENTIAL MATERIAL HERE either.
